For deciding the reference U/s 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 r/w statement U/s 19 of the Act sent by the Land Acquisition Collector (for short 'LAC'), the relevant dates and facts which are necessary for adjudication in the present matter are being given herein-under:-
i) Date of notification U/s 4 of the Act : 14.10.2005 ii) Date of notification U/s 6 of the Act : 05.10.2006 iii) Date of award : 22.07.2008
iv) Area of the locality : Jhilmil Tahirpur v) Project : Construction of RUB on Road No.58 & 64 at GT Road, Shahdara Delhi.

The facts leading to the filing of the present petition are that the notification dated 14.10.2005 under Section 4 of the L.A. Act, 1894 was issued by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as "LAC") for acquisition of land/properties for the purpose of construction of Road Under Bridge [RUB] on Road Nos.58 & 64 at G.T. Road Shahdara situated in Village Jhilmil Tahirpur, which was followed by the Notification dated 05.10.2006 under Section 6 of L.A. Act,
1894.

The LAC has mentioned in the award that the properties under acquisition were situated close to Shahdara flyover and have commercial activities in the vicinity, the properties were serving both commercial as well as residential purposes.

However at the time of assessment of market value, the LAC has relied upon certain sale deeds and fixed the market value of the acquired properties @
Rs.1973 per sq. mtrs. after deducting 30% of the total value for the cost of structures.
A total area of 11 bighas 5 biswas was acquired vide above award.

Further solatium at the rate of 30% of market value alongwith the additional amount @ 12% of market value w.e.f. 14.10.2005 to 17.11.2006 [date of granting stay by the Hon'ble High Court] and secondly w.e.f. 18.05.2008 [when the stay was vacated] to 26.07.2008 [date of award] was allowed apart from cost of structure appended to the said land and statutory interest under Section 34 of Act.
Thus, an Award for total amount of Rs.6,32,01,899/- was passed by the LAC.
4 Being aggrieved from the lesser rate fi Xed by LAC for the acquired land, the petitioner filed a petition under Section 18 of L.A. Act, 1894 before the LAC.

The LAC sent the present reference petition to this court for adjudication and subsequently the present case was listed for trial and finally the present matter has come before this Court for final adjudication.

Since all the matters pertaining to the said area i.e. Jhilmil Tahirpur were remanded back by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi for adducing of additional evidence by all the parties, the present reference petition was also sent for adducing of additional evidence in this court by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide its order dated 21.12.2017 passed in LA (A) No. 271/16.
5

In the present case, since the petition U/s 18 of the LA Act was forwarded by the LAC earlier, this case has already finished its first round of litigation and thereafter my Ld. Predecessor enhanced the Sandesh Chawla And Ors vs Uoi And Ors on 6 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118906881/

Union of India & PWD bearing LAC No.5-A/11 whose property was also acquired by the same notification and my Ld. Predecessor was pleased to enhance the market value from Rs.1973 per sq. mtrs. to Rs.20605/- per sq. mtrs. and thereafter, the matter was impugned by the parties before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.

sentences.text: 6 In the reference petition, the petitioners contended that they are the co-owners of the land plot no.9, Gali No.2, Friends Colony Industrial Area Shahdara, Delhi forming part of Khasra No.1141/320/306/7, measuring area 10 biswas (approximately 502 sq. yards), Jhilmil Tahirpur also known as Friends Colony Industrial Area Gali no.2, Shdhara, Delhi duly approved by Government of Industries Master Plans, in which petitioner no.1 is running industry as proprietor of last more than 20 years.
It is further contended that the petitioner no.1 carried out extensive development in the land by raising construction and setting up machinery for carrying out the industrial activities.
It is further averred that the petitioners have filed the present reference with respect to entire share of land in question, notified and acquired vide abovesaid award.

The petitioners had received notice under Section 9 & 10 of the LA Act dated 09.11.2006 and they had filed their claims in respect of their shares in the abovesaid land under protest and have claimed @ Rs.70,000/- per sq. yards for their shares of land with other claims as per LA Act but the LAC had not considered their claims and determined the market value of the land according to the government minimum rates.

It is further averred that the LAC has assessed the compensation of the land at a very low rate and as such the petitioners aggrieved from the award have preferred the present reference petition within limitation.
The petitioners described the compensation amount as inadequate and unjustified and demanded compensation at the rate of Rs.70,000/- per sq. yard for land, Rs.25 lacs for structure and other compensation/damage under different heads.
7
During the pendency of the petition, petitioner no.1 expired and his legal heirs were brought on record.

8 Both the respondents i.e. Union of India and Public Works Department contested the matter and described the awarded compensation amount as justified, correct and reasonable and requested to dismiss the petition of the petitioners.

9 After completion of pleadings following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 01.06.2013:-
1
What was the fair market value of the land in question on the date of notification u/s 4 of the Land Acquisition Act?
OPP 3 Whether the petitioners are entitled to enhancement?
OPP 3 Relief.

10 In earlier proceedings ld. Counsel for petitioners by giving statement adopted the evidence led in case titled as D.N. Sharma Vs. UOI, LAC no.5-A/11 which was treated as a main case and then he closed the evidence of the petitioners.

sentences.text: On the other hand ld. counsel for respondent no.2 argued that the compensation assessed by the LAC is sufficient and reasonable and it reflects the true market value prevailing at the time of the notification under section 4 of the LA Act.

He further submitted that he is also relying upon the certified copies of sale deeds which were relied upon by the LAC in its award whereby he has determined the cost of land under acquisition and he requested to dismiss the reference petition with costs.
20 Ld. counsel for respondent no.1 did not file written arguments nor addressed oral arguments despite giving sufficient time.
21 I have heard arguments on behalf of parties and also perused the record.

On perusal of record,
my issue-wise finding is as follows:-
22
Both these issue are being taken up together for disposal being inter connected.
Onus to prove these issues was upon the petitioners.

23 First and foremost, for the ascertainment of the actual market value, it is necessary to consider the admissions made by all the parties in the pleadings as well as in their evidence led in support of their contentions.
The relevant portion of the award announced by the LAC is reproduced herein-under:-
"To arrive at a fair market value, the locality of the site, the situation of the area, the quality, potentiality and use of land are to be kept in mind.
The properties/land under acquisition are situated close to Shahdara flyover and have commercial activities in the vicinity.
The said properties are serving both commercial as well as residential purposes."

24 The LAC has assessed the market value on the basis of four sale deeds which though being proximate to the date of notification U/s 4 but do not specify as to whether the said properties were situated in the residential areas or commercial areas.
The respondent no.2 has also relied on the same sale deeds which were relied upon by the LAC in its award whereby he has determined the cost of land under acquisition.

In the four sale deeds relied upon by the LAC, there is a great variation in the market value arrived at per sq. mtr. in the sale deed dated 25.11.2004 and 16.03.2005.
25
I have perused the said sale deeds Ex.RW1/1 (colly.).

The first sale deed dated 25.11.2004 cannot be relied upon by this court since it has already been mentioned in the sale deed that the physical possession of the property under sale was already with the vendee much prior to its sale and therefore could not be taken into consideration that it was executed between a willing purchaser and willing seller.
The said sale was clearly a distressed sale and cannot be taken into consideration.

26 The next sale deed relied upon by the PWD dated 23.06.2005 could also not be relied since the said sale pertains to a residential plot of land and the properties under acquisition were clearly commercial in nature.

sentences.text: The third sale deed relied upon by the PWD dated 22.06.2005 can also not be taken into consideration since it pertains to part of a particular property and was also in respect of a residential house situated in the interior of Dilshad Garden.
28 The last sale deed relied by the PWD dated 16.03.2005 also pertains to only a part of the property and there is no mention of the fact whether the property is commercial or residential.
The PWD chose not to examine any vendor or vendee and for this reason, the sale deeds relied upon by PWD cannot be taken into consideration for the assessment of the market value.
29 The sale deeds Ex.RW1/1 (colly.) relied upon by the Land Acquisition Collector are also of no relevance in the present case in view of the reasons stated above.
They do not give any specification with respect to their proximity with the acquired properties and have rather not even been filed in the present case.
The sale deeds Ex.RW1/1 (colly.) relied upon by the collector do not give any reason for me to hold that they were genuine or bonafide in any manner.

30 As per section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, the market value of the acquired properties is liable to be ascertained/ determined as on the date of issuance of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act which in this particular case is 14.10.2005.

The petitioner has duly stated that the rate of Rs.1973/-
per sq. mtrs. as assessed by the LAC is extremely meagre for the prime commercial property of the petitioner.
For the assessment of the correct market value, ld.

Counsel for petitioner has relied the judgment passed by this court in case titled as Rakesh Kumar Gupta Vs. UOI & Anr., LAC No.3/16 which pertains to the present award, in which other claimant has relied upon the schedule of market rates issued by the Ministry of Land & Development Office published in the year 2018 i.e.
02.05.2017 as Ex.PW8/1.

sentences.text: As already stated above, the LAC has observed that the properties/land under acquisition are situated close to Shahdara flyover and have commercial activities in the vicinity.
The said properties are serving both commercial as well as residential purposes.

To assess the market value of the land,
the LAC has considered certain sale deeds which I have already discussed earlier.

It is ironical that in award No.2/07-08 pertaining to the same area i.e. Jhilmil Tahirpur, the LAC has based the said award on the basis of schedule of market rates, however in this very award which was passed almost six months subsequently, he has stated that these rates are not applicable for arrival of fair market value.

32 Section 23 of L.A. Act, 1894 provides that in order to determine the amount of compensation to be awarded for land acquired under this Act, the Court shall take into consideration the market value of the land on the date of publication of notification under section 4 (1).

33 In Kapil Mehra Vs. UOI (MANU/SC/0947/2014), the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that market value is ordinarily the price the property may fetch in the open market if sold by a willing seller unaffected by the special needs of a particular purchase, and where definite material is not forthcoming either in the shape of sales of similar lands in the neighborhood at or about the date of notification under Section 4 (1) or otherwise, other sale instances as well as other evidence have to be considered.

It has been further observed that for the purpose of fi Xation of fair and reasonable Sandesh Chawla And Ors vs Uoi And Ors on 6 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118906881/
6 market value of any type of land, abnormally high value or abnormally low value sales should be carefully discarded.

34 In Karnataka Urban Water Supply & Drainage Board & Ors. vs. K.S. Gangadharappa & Anr.
MANU/SC/0598/2009, the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed as under:-
"11.

It can be broadly stated that the element of speculation is reduced to minimum if the underlying principles of fiXation of market value with reference to comparable sales are made as:-
a. when sale is within a reasonable time of the date of notification under Section 4 (1);
b. it should be a bona fide transaction; c. it should be of the land acquired or of the land adjacent to the land acquired; and d. it should possess similar advantages."
35

The respondent no.1 on the other hand has also admitted that the award announced by the Land Acquisition Collector is true and correct and reflects the actual market value of the property of the petitioner.
By admitting the award, respondent no.1 has also admitted the location and potentiality of the acquired properties to be in the area of Jhilmil Tahirpur itself and to be commercial.

36 During the proceedings pending with respect to the present reference petition, the Ministry of Urban Affairs & Development itself published the revised rates dated 02.05.2017 with respect to the various localities in Delhi w.e.f. 01.04.2000 onwards.

37 The Hon'ble Apex Court has held in Lal Chand Vs. UOI (supra) that the distance between the two properties, the nature and situation of the property, proximity to the village or a road and several other factors may all be relevant in determining the market value.
Mere production of some exemplar deeds without 'connecting' the subject matter of the instrument, to the acquired lands will be of little assistance in determining the market value.

38 In Anjani Molu Dessai Vs State of Goa & Anr, 2010 (2010) 13 SCC 710, the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed as under:-
"13.

sentences.text:
The legal position is that even where there are several exemplars with reference to similar lands, usually the highest of the e X emplars, which is a bona fide Sandesh Chawla And Ors vs Uoi And Ors on 6 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118906881/
7 transaction, will be considered.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where however there are several sales of similar lands whose prices range in a narrow bandwidth, the average thereof can be taken, as representing the market price.

But where the values disclosed in respect of two sales are markedly different, it can only lead to an inference that they are with reference to dissimilar lands or that the lower value sale is on account of under-valuation or other price depressing reasons."

39 It is again relevant to note herein that the sale deeds mentioned by the LAC in the award itself pose a great variation in the market value arrived in the said sale deeds and therefore they very well lead to the inference that they are with respect to dissimilar land or distressed sale deeds.
40

In Ali Mohammad Beigh & Ors. Vs. State of J&K reported in AIR 2017 SC 1518, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that "when the acquired lands are identical and similar and the acquisition is for the same purpose, it would not be proper to discriminate between the land owners unless there are strong reasons."

sentences.text:
This court has already enhanced the market value of other property holders whose properties have been acquired vide award No.2/07-08 vide judgment in LAC Nos.7/20, 14/20 and 15/20 titled as Monika Gupta Vs. UOI, Vinod Kumar Gupta Vs UOI and Sunil Kumar Jain Vs UOI respectively,
in which this court has been pleased to fix the market value of the properties acquired vide above award @ Rs.48,000/- per sq. meters and the petitioner is therefore liable to receive enhancement in terms of aforesaid judgments passed by this court after due deduction of 6% from the said value since though the present award was passed subsequent to award No.2/07-08, the date of notification was however six months prior to the said date.
42

Since this court has already enhanced the market value of other property holders whose properties have been acquired vide award No.2/07-08 vide judgement bearing LAC No.7/20, 14/20 and 15/20 titled as Monika Gupta Vs. UOI, Sunil Kumar Jain Vs UOI and Vinod Kumar Gupta Vs UOI respectively, it is held that the petitioner is also liable to receive enhancement in terms of aforesaid judgments passed by this court after due deduction of 6% from the said value since though the present award was passed subsequent to award No.2/07-08, the date of notification was however six months prior to the said date.

43 In view of the earlier discussion, I hereby determine the market value of the properties acquired vide the present award to be Rs.45,120/- per sq. mtrs. as on the date of notification i.e. 14.10.2005 being six months prior to the date of notification of award No.2/07-08 Jhilmil Tahirpur Delhi.
44 The LAC has awarded an amount of Rs.1973/- per sq. mtrs.
A perusal of the file also reveals that the petitioner has never received any amount over and above the awarded amount of compensation of Rs.1973/- per sq. mtrs.

Therefore, the petitioner is now entitled to the market value @
Rs.45,120/- per sq. mtrs.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled to a further enhancement of Rs.43,147/- per sq. mtrs. over and above Rs.1973/- per sq. mtrs.

sentences.text: RELIEF 45

In view of the findings of issue No.1 & 2, the petitioner is entitled to the market value @
Rs.45,120/- per sq. mtrs. as on 14.10.2005.

In addition, the petitioner would also be entitled to all statutory benefits i.e. 30% solatium on the market value in view of the compulsory nature of acquisition U/s 23 (2) of the LA Act and an additional amount of 12% per annum on the market value from the date of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act till date of possession or award whichever is earlier as per section 23 (1A) of the LA Act.

Besides this the petitioner would also be entitled to interest on the enhanced amount of compensation @ 9% per annum from the date of dispossession till expiry of one year and thereafter @ 15% per annum till the date of payment of the balance amount.
Enhanced compensation is awarded to the petitioner in the ratio which has been determined in separate case u/s 30-31 of the LA Act.

26 The next sale deed relied upon by the PWD dated 23.06.2005 could also not be relied since the said sale pertains to a residential plot of land and the properties under acquisition were clearly commercial in nature.
The third sale deed relied upon by the PWD dated 22.06.2005 can also not be taken into consideration since it pertains to part of a particular property and was also in respect of a residential house situated in the interior of Dilshad Garden.
28 The last sale deed relied by the PWD dated 16.03.2005 also pertains to only a part of the property and there is no mention of the fact whether the property is commercial or residential.
The PWD chose not to examine any vendor or vendee and for this reason, the sale deeds relied upon by PWD cannot be taken into consideration for the assessment of the market value.
They do not give any specification with respect to their proximity with the acquired properties and have rather not even been filed in the present case.
The sale deeds Ex.RW1/1 (colly.) relied upon by the collector do not give any reason for me to hold that they were genuine or bonafide in any manner.
30 As per section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, the market value of the acquired properties is liable to be ascertained/ determined as on the date of issuance of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act which in this particular case is 14.10.2005.
Counsel for petitioner has relied the judgment passed by this court in case titled as Rakesh Kumar Gupta Vs. UOI & Anr., LAC No.3/16 which pertains to the present award, in which other claimant has relied upon the schedule of market rates issued by the Ministry of Land & Development Office published in the year 2018 i.e.
02.05.2017 as Ex.PW8/1.
31
34 In Karnataka Urban Water Supply & Drainage Board & Ors. vs. K.S. Gangadharappa & Anr.
MANU/SC/0598/2009, the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed as under:-
"11.
38 In Anjani Molu Dessai Vs State of Goa & Anr, 2010 (2010) 13 SCC 710, the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed as under:-
"13.
In view of the said judgments, the petitioner claims the same amount of compensation as assessed in case titled Rakesh Kumar Gupta Vs. Union of India & Anr., LAC no.
3/16.
41
opennyai_summary.decision:
43 In view of the earlier discussion, I hereby determine the market value of the properties acquired vide the present award to be Rs.45,120/- per sq. mtrs. as on the date of notification i.e. 14.10.2005 being six months prior to the date of notification of award No.2/07-08 Jhilmil Tahirpur Delhi.
44 The LAC has awarded an amount of Rs.1973/- per sq. mtrs.
Therefore, the petitioner is now entitled to the market value @
Rs.45,120/- per sq. mtrs.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled to a further enhancement of Rs.43,147/- per sq. mtrs. over and above Rs.1973/- per sq. mtrs.
[1973 + 43147 = Rs.45120/- per sq.
Sandesh Chawla And Ors vs Uoi And Ors on 6 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118906881/
8 mtrs.].
RELIEF 45
In view of the findings of issue No.1 & 2, the petitioner is entitled to the market value @
Rs.45,120/- per sq. mtrs. as on 14.10.2005.
In addition, the petitioner would also be entitled to all statutory benefits i.e. 30% solatium on the market value in view of the compulsory nature of acquisition U/s 23 (2) of the LA Act and an additional amount of 12% per annum on the market value from the date of notification U/s 4 of the LA Act till date of possession or award whichever is earlier as per section 23 (1A) of the LA Act.
Besides this the petitioner would also be entitled to interest on the enhanced amount of compensation @ 9% per annum from the date of dispossession till expiry of one year and thereafter @ 15% per annum till the date of payment of the balance amount.
Enhanced compensation is awarded to the petitioner in the ratio which has been determined in separate case u/s 30-31 of the LA Act.
46 Reference is answered accordingly.
Parties to bear their own costs.
Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
47 A copy of this judgment be sent to the concerned LAC for information and necessary compliance within three months of its receipt.
File be consigned to Record Room as per rules.
